title: Recipe 10 — Browser Agent (vision grounding, and the trust surface that comes with it)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Recipe 10 is the largest trust-surface expansion of any target shape: one Click on the wrong button is the whole incident.”
beats.script: Recipe 10 is the largest trust-surface expansion of any target shape: one Click on the wrong button is the whole incident. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens 10 browser agent.md now. Keep this artifact in view: it is the concrete evidence behind the behavior this beat describes.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.
beats.script: Live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take. [[pause:900ms]] The driver clears live slash crewhaus.yaml in the scratch workspace now, giving this take a repeatable starting point without changing the committed example.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beats — the agent model and the grounding model both call out.
beats.script: Sources demos/.env for the run beats — the agent model and the grounding model both call out. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Operator-supplied demos/.env.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec — pixels, not selectors

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “target: browser” — one of only two shapes crewhaus run drives straight from the spec.
beats.script: “target: browser” — one of only two shapes crewhaus run drives straight from the spec. [[pause:900ms]] Watch the driver type lines 86 through 87 of 10 browser agent.md, rebuilding live slash crewhaus.yaml from a known state. The slice comes from committed source, so the fresh file exactly matches the example this take is introducing.

beats.label: Add the agent block
beats.cue: “Screenshot, find, click, screenshot again. The verifying screenshot is the whole difference between automation and guessing.”
beats.script: Screenshot, find, click, screenshot again. The verifying screenshot is the whole difference between automation and guessing. [[pause:900ms]] Watch lines 88 through 94 of 10 browser agent.md become the next block of live slash crewhaus.yaml. Because the bytes come from the checked-in source, the onscreen result is the exact material the verifier exercises.

beats.label: Add the driver and the grounding model
beats.cue: “The viewport is the coordinate space every Click is expressed in — that is why coordinates are reproducible across runs. And startUrl is baked in at compile time: there is no --start-url flag.”
beats.script: The viewport is the coordinate space every Click is expressed in — that is why coordinates are reproducible across runs. And startUrl is baked in at compile time: there is no --start-url flag. [[pause:900ms]] Watch lines 95 through 101 of 10 browser agent.md become the next block of live slash crewhaus.yaml. Because the bytes come from the checked-in source, the onscreen result is the exact material the verifier exercises.

beats.label: Allow the destructive tools
beats.cue: “Click, Type, Key and Scroll all declare destructive. Under mode: default they prompt on every call — so a browser agent that runs unattended needs these rules, with the tightest patterns you can live with.”
beats.script: Click, Type, Key and Scroll all declare destructive. Under mode: default they prompt on every call — so a browser agent that runs unattended needs these rules, with the tightest patterns you can live with. [[pause:900ms]] Watch lines 102 through 116 of 10 browser agent.md become the next block of live slash crewhaus.yaml. Because the bytes come from the checked-in source, the onscreen result is the exact material the verifier exercises.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”
beats.script: Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Lint: clean — no findings.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Driver, viewport, start URL, grounding model and all six rules — 51 lines, and every one of them auditable.”
beats.script: Driver, viewport, start URL, grounding model and all six rules — 51 lines, and every one of them auditable. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Prints the IR for target browser (51 lines).

verify.note: prints the IR for target browser (51 lines)

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps and boots it: GREEN, and the gate it reaches is the missing --prompt.”
beats.script: --check asserts the shape, installs the deps and boots it: GREEN, and the gate it reaches is the missing --prompt. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. GREEN — assertion ok (10 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the initial --prompt gate.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (10 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the initial --prompt gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: “About a hundred lines you could have written by hand. Nothing magic — same as Recipe 01.”
beats.script: About a hundred lines you could have written by hand. Nothing magic — same as Recipe 01. [[pause:1.2s]] The editor opens live slash dist slash agent.ts now. This is the source or generated artifact behind the current step; focus on the details the first chunk called out.

beats.label: Count the tools it wired
beats.cue: “Navigate, screen capture, mouse and keyboard, vision grounding, plus the catalog. Five imports, seven registered tools.”
beats.script: Navigate, screen capture, mouse and keyboard, vision grounding, plus the catalog. Five imports, seven registered tools. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. 5 matches: tool-navigate, tool-screen-capture, tool-mouse-keyboard, tool-vision-grounding, tool-catalog.

verify.note: 5 matches: tool-navigate, tool-screen-capture, tool-mouse-keyboard, tool-vision-grounding, tool-catalog

beats.label: Read the emitted rule set
beats.cue: “Six alwaysAllow rules — and the bundle registers seven tools. Navigate is the one nobody named, so under mode: default it resolves to ask, and a --prompt run cannot ask. That is a deny you would otherwise find at runtime; the starter's spec adds the seventh rule for exactly this reason.”
beats.script: Six alwaysAllow rules — and the bundle registers seven tools. Navigate is the one nobody named, so under mode: default it resolves to ask, and a --prompt run cannot ask. That is a deny you would otherwise find at runtime; the starter's spec adds the seventh rule for exactly this reason. [[pause:1.5s]] This command is replayable offline, so its result is part of the repository's machine-checked demo contract. One match plus 10 lines: flag/settings empty, then the six yaml rules Screenshot → Scroll. Navigate is absent from the recipe's spec, deliberately reported here rather than glossed over.

verify.note: one match plus 10 lines: flag/settings empty, then the six yaml rules Screenshot → Scroll. Navigate is absent from the recipe's spec, deliberately reported here rather than glossed over.

beats.label: Boot it with no task
beats.cue: “Deliberate non-zero, exit 2: no --prompt and nothing on stdin, so it stops before it ever launches chromium. The task is an argument, not a config file.”
beats.script: Deliberate non-zero, exit 2: no --prompt and nothing on stdin, so it stops before it ever launches chromium. The task is an argument, not a config file. [[pause:1.5s]] The nonzero result is intentional: this command expects exit code 2. Measured exit 2: `no prompt (pass --prompt <text> or pipe stdin)`.

verify.note: measured exit 2: `no prompt (pass --prompt <text> or pipe stdin)`. stdin is closed explicitly so the beat behaves the same on camera as it does here; the key is scrubbed because the Setup group already sourced .env into this shell.

beats.label: Add playwright to the bundle
beats.cue: “The computer-use driver declares playwright as an optional peer, so the bundle install never pulls 150 megabytes you might not need.”
beats.script: The computer-use driver declares playwright as an optional peer, so the bundle install never pulls 150 megabytes you might not need. [[pause:1.5s]] No credentials are involved in this check; a clean exit confirms the local path behaves as described. Installs playwright@1.6x into the bundle's own node_modules.

verify.note: installs playwright@1.6x into the bundle's own node_modules

beats.label: Show what the browser install would fetch
beats.cue: “Chrome for Testing, the headless shell and ffmpeg — pinned versions, exact URLs, and a cache path outside the repo. Downloads nothing.”
beats.script: Chrome for Testing, the headless shell and ffmpeg — pinned versions, exact URLs, and a cache path outside the repo. Downloads nothing. [[pause:1.5s]] The terminal is exercising the real implementation locally here, and the verifier expects a successful exit. Prints version, install location and download URL for each artifact; --dry-run fetches nothing.

verify.note: prints version, install location and download URL for each artifact; --dry-run fetches nothing

beats.label: Install chromium for real
beats.cue: [manual] “~150MB of browser binary. Do this once before the take, not on camera.”
beats.script: ~150MB of browser binary. Do this once before the take, not on camera. [[pause:1.8s]] This step hands control to the operator for the interactive portion. Large binary download; the verifier never runs it — the --dry-run beat above proves the invocation form.

verify.note: large binary download; the verifier never runs it — the --dry-run beat above proves the invocation form

groups.title: One more thing · drive the fixture

beats.label: Start the fixture page
beats.cue: [manual] “A single page with a green Submit button whose marker flips from PENDING to BROW_SMOKE_OK when it is clicked. Leave this running in its own terminal.”
beats.script: A single page with a green Submit button whose marker flips from PENDING to BROW_SMOKE_OK when it is clicked. Leave this running in its own terminal. [[pause:1.8s]] This is the hands-on portion of the take, so the operator completes it while the driver keeps the context visible. Long-lived dev server on 127.0.0.1:7325 — the spec's startUrl. Needs a second terminal and a human to stop it.

verify.note: long-lived dev server on 127.0.0.1:7325 — the spec's startUrl. Needs a second terminal and a human to stop it.

beats.label: Give the agent the task
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Screenshot, FindElement on the green Submit button, Click its center, screenshot to verify. Chromium runs headless in 0.4.x, so the JSON event stream is the take: browser_start, navigated, browser_done.”
beats.script: Screenshot, FindElement on the green Submit button, Click its center, screenshot to verify. Chromium runs headless in 0.4.x, so the JSON event stream is the take: browser_start, navigated, browser_done. [[pause:1.8s]] The demo crosses into its live path at this point; with the required credentials loaded, the real runtime performs the work. Browser is one of the two shapes crewhaus run supports; needs Anthropic credentials for both the agent and the grounding model, and the fixture beat above to be running.
beats.command: crewhaus run live/crewhaus.yaml --prompt "Click the green Submit button on the page."

verify.note: browser is one of the two shapes crewhaus run supports; needs Anthropic credentials for both the agent and the grounding model, and the fixture beat above to be running

beats.label: Or run the whole thing as one smoke
beats.cue: [needs-key] “The section-25 smoke boots the fixture, compiles the example, runs the agent, asserts the page really says BROW_SMOKE_OK, then proves the permission floor by re-running a variant with no allowAll rules and checking the click was denied. Same path CI takes.”
beats.script: The section-25 smoke boots the fixture, compiles the example, runs the agent, asserts the page really says BROW_SMOKE_OK, then proves the permission floor by re-running a variant with no allowAll rules and checking the click was denied. Same path CI takes. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay.
